I read the structure region by region, from left to right.

**Left end.** An indole is attached at C3 to a CH2, which leads to a CH bearing the NH and a butyl chain. The chain from the CH is CH2-CH2-CH2-CH3, and the drawing shows it zigzagging down to the terminal carbon. That makes the fragment indol-3-yl-CH2-CH(NH-)-CH2CH2CH2CH3, a 1-(indol-3-yl)hexan-2-yl group. The CH is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

**Amide and thiazole.** The NH is acylated by a carbonyl on C5 of a thiazole. The thiazole runs C5, C4, N3, C2, S1, and C2 carries the piperazine nitrogen.

**Piperazine and linker.** The other piperazine nitrogen is attached to CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-, which is five oxygens in total. Counting from the image: N-CH2CH2-O (the first O), CH2CH2-O (the second), CH2CH2-O (the third), CH2CH2-O (the fourth), CH2CH2-O (the fifth) attached to the aryl ring. The last oxygen is the aryl ether.

**Right end.** The aryl ring is part of a phthalimide, and the ether oxygen sits on the ring at position 5. The imide nitrogen is attached to C3 of a 2,6-dioxopiperidine.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Indole and side chain: c1ccc2c(c1)c(CC(CCCC)NC(=O)...)c[nH]2
- Thiazole: c1cnc(s1)N2CCN(CC2)...
- Linker: CCOCCOCCOCCOCCOc
- Phthalimide: c3ccc4c(c3)C(=O)N(C4=O)C5CCC(=O)NC5=O
